title: 16 bugs, one storefront
simple: This is the Agentic Personas storefront from the ECI interview. It shipped with 16 hidden bugs. This tutorial walks through each one on the real app: what a user would have seen, how we found it, and how it was fixed.

title: Nothing builds: shared package fails to compile
simple: The whole project would not build, so nothing else could even be tested. We stopped the compiler from picking up an unrelated type package.
how: error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'testing-library__jest-dom'. (findings/baseline-build.log, BUILD_EXIT=2)
found: First command run on the clone: pnpm build. It stopped at @acme/shared.
fix: tsc auto-includes every @types package it can see in ancestor node_modules. A stub for testing-library__jest-dom had no types, so the compiler failed on a package the code never uses. Shared needs no ambient types, so the fix is to say so explicitly (types: []) instead of installing a dependency to satisfy a file we do not import.
codeAfter: "types": [] so only declared types are used

title: Price filter returned the wrong items
simple: Asking for personas costing at least $80 also returned cheaper ones.
how: GET /personas?minPrice=80 returned items at or below the minimum before the fix; after, only items from p-002 upward.
found: Read the personas route and its db query while sweeping API behaviour.
fix: A filter named minPrice must keep items at or above the value. The comparison used <= instead of >=. One character, but it silently inverts the feature.

title: Login response was missing the username
simple: After signing in, the app did not receive the user's name, which the shared contract requires.
how: POST /auth/login returned a user without username. After the fix it returns user.username (tester in the smoke run).
found: Compared the login handler's response object with the AuthResponse schema in packages/shared.
fix: The shared Zod schema is the contract between web and API. The handler built the user object by hand and left one field out. Fix at the source, not by loosening the schema.

title: Browser could not delete cart or favorite items
simple: Removing something from the cart or favorites failed in the browser even though the API itself worked.
how: The allowed-methods list did not include DELETE, so the browser blocked the preflight request.
found: Read the CORS configuration in the server entry file.
fix: Direct curl calls succeed because CORS is only enforced by browsers. That is why this bug hides from API-only testing. Add DELETE to the allowed methods.

title: Anyone could delete someone else's cart item
simple: A signed-in user could remove another user's cart item. This is a security hole.
how: DELETE skipped the item.userId === userId check that the PUT route has.
found: Compared DELETE /cart/:itemId with PUT /cart/:itemId, which did check ownership.
fix: The sibling route already had the right guard, which proves the intent. Return 404 (not 403) for someone else's item so item ids cannot be probed.
codeBefore: DELETE removed any item by id

title: Checkout left the cart full
simple: After paying, the items were still in the cart.
how: After the fix: checkout returns 201, then GET /cart returns an empty list with total 0.
found: Followed the checkout route from order creation to its end.
fix: The order was created but nothing cleared the user's cart. Add the clear call after the order is saved, not before, so a failed order keeps the cart.

title: Auth was off by default, so cart and checkout crashed
simple: Cart, favorites and checkout crashed for signed-in users because the server never checked the login token.
how: Without a token /cart now returns 401; with a token it returns 200. Before, the handlers dereferenced a missing user.
found: Smoke-testing cart routes: request.user was undefined.
fix: Auth enforcement was opt-in (ENFORCE_AUTH had to equal the string true), so by default the verify hook was skipped. A secure default is the correct behaviour: enforce unless ENFORCE_AUTH is explicitly false. This also changed what the web client must send, so it was cross-checked by the web smoke.

title: Web typecheck failed
simple: The web app failed its own type check, for the same hidden-type reason plus one unexported type.
how: TS2688 (stray @types), then TS4023: SearchParams is used by the generated route tree but not exported.
fix: Two separate causes behind one red result. Fixing the first revealed the second, which is why this is one commit with both changes.

title: Prices displayed 100 times too high
how: The card computed persona.price * 100 before formatting. After the fix the smoke run showed normal prices around $49.99.
fix: The API already returns dollars. Multiplying is a unit conversion that does not belong here. Format only.

title: Search, filter and sort never refreshed the list
simple: Choosing a specialty or typing a search did nothing, because the page kept showing the first result.
how: After the fix the smoke run showed the specialty filter changing the list from 15 results to 4.
found: Read the browse route's data query.
fix: The query cache key was a constant, so every filter hit the same cache entry. The key must include the query string, since TanStack Query refetches when the key changes.

title: Favorite heart did the opposite
simple: Clicking the heart on a non-favorite tried to delete it, and clicking a favorite tried to add it again.
how: A stray ! on isFavorited sent DELETE when not favorited and POST when favorited.
found: Read the persona page's favorite toggle.
fix: One extra negation inverted the condition. Removed it. No other lines needed to change.

title: Favorites page and persona page fought over one cache entry
simple: Opening a persona could corrupt the favorites list, and it asked for favorites while signed out.
how: The same cache key held a list of ids on one page and an object on the other, and there was no signed-in guard (a 401 when signed out).
found: Read the favorites queries on both pages side by side.
fix: Two different data shapes under one key is a cache collision. Give the ids their own key and only run the query when a user exists.

title: Logging out did not log you out
simple: After logout, reloading the page signed you back in, and the next person could see the previous user's cached data.
how: Logout cleared in-memory state only, so the token stayed in localStorage. The smoke run confirms the token is gone and stays gone after reload.
found: Read the auth provider's logout function.
fix: Auth state lives in three places: React state, localStorage and the query cache. Logout must clear all three.

title: Cart badge never updated
simple: The number on the cart icon stayed stale after adding or removing items.
how: The badge used the key cart-count, but the mutations invalidate the key cart, so the badge never refetched. The smoke run showed the badge following each change.
found: Read the navbar and the cart mutations side by side.
fix: TanStack Query invalidates by key prefix. Renaming the key to cart,count makes the existing invalidation reach it, with no new plumbing.

title: Cart quantity could go to zero or below
simple: The minus button let you push a quantity to 0 or negative.
how: The minus button was styled as disabled but never given the disabled attribute. In the smoke run minus is disabled at 1.
fix: Styling is not behaviour. Set disabled when quantity is 1 or less.

title: Star ratings drew the wrong partial fill
simple: Half stars on one card could show another card's fill.
how: Every partial star used the same SVG gradient id half, so the first gradient in the page won for all cards.
fix: SVG ids are global to the document. Use React's useId so each star gets its own gradient.

title: All 16 fixed
simple: The project builds, type-checks, and a headless browser walked every main flow with zero errors: register, browse, filter, favorite, cart, checkout, logout.
